Here $I$ is the identity operator, which leaves every array unchanged.

gaps.quote: multiplying by $-\varepsilon_w$ again removes the sign
gaps.note: Wrong sign. The route multiplies by eps_w in {+1,-1}; removing it means multiplying by eps_w again (eps_w^2=1), as the paper does ('Negate those outputs' only where the sign is -1, paper lines 146 and 1312). Multiplying by -eps_w would leave the factor -1 on every role, and would flip scratch roles (sign +1), contradicting the next sentence that scratch needs no correction.

gaps.quote: its operator is $D_\nu$, however many gates it passes through
gaps.note: Inconsistent with the page's own formula: a route applies eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}, so with source frame I and sink frame D_nu the operator is eps_w D_nu, equal to D_nu only when the sign is +1.

gaps.quote: on arrays indexed by the common address set
gaps.note: The page never defines the common address set: that each role stream (V/W bits) has the same local address set, so arrays on different wires can be combined pointwise and one frame can act on them. The reader cannot tell what the frames act on.

gaps.term: network structure (wires, gates, sources, sinks, edges, banks)
gaps.quote: Each source, gate and sink $\nu$ carries an invertible linear operator
gaps.note: The page never explains the network's structure: that each wire has a source, then the gates touching it in time order, then a sink, with edges joining consecutive vertices (paper lines 660-668), nor what 'two banks' of exchanged values are. Source, sink, node, edge and route are used without definition.

gaps.quote: The intermediate frames cancel, and the route applies only its endpoint operator.
gaps.note: The telescoping product covers only the edge operators. The page never says that the gates' action sits between them and is a pointwise linear map commuting with the common frame, nor that the supplied input is interpreted through the inverse source frame (paper lines 141-142, 805-824). So the claim that the whole network applies eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1} is not derived from what the page gives.
